question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 2+5\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{(-3)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 1+5\cdot 0+1\cdot 2}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 0+5\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ 

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}\,x}{‖x‖\,‖{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x‖} \\  & =\frac{(-3)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 3}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{18}{\sqrt{36}\sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{18}{6\cdot 3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
